summary:
R4 remains the model's undisputed engine right now — 46-18 (72%) on trends and a perfect 25-7, +20.0u strong-play mark across every window since inception, though it's worth flagging that same rating is riding a 4L streak on hitting (39-25 season) and bullpen_fatigue sits at just 47-34. R1/R2/R3 are all humming on trends at 57% over the last 14 days (108-80, n=188), and R2's strong plays have been the hottest of the trio short-term: 76% (29-9, +18.0u) over the last 7 days. The trends+runs combo remains the best category pairing on the board at 57.6% (269-198), so any game where trends and runs both point the same direction deserves extra weight today.

On the slate, four-rating consensus dominates — 12 of 15 games have all four models aligned, and that's where the strong-play units have been made. TBR @ DET is the sharpest signal of the day, with all four ratings stacked on TBR by -2.06 to -2.21, squarely in strong-play territory and lining up with TBR's excellent 26-12 (68%) record when picked, including a blistering 19-5 (79%, +23.0u) mark on strong plays specifically — this is the kind of number the model has cashed all year. WSN vs COL is another full-consensus lean (+1.76 to +2.48), while LAD @ ATL sees the model fade the Dodgers by as much as -1.97 despite LAD's stellar 22-9 (71%) season track record when liked — worth noting the ratings are picking Atlanta here, not LAD, so that strong number doesn't apply. BOS @ MIA is a lean the other way, fading Boston (-0.72 to -1.08) despite BOS being the model's best team-when-liked play at 79% (33-9) and 77% strong — but that record is for games where BOS is the pick, and here BOS is the fade side. The two split games, MIL @ NYM and PHI @ SEA, show real model disagreement (R2 flips to NYM, R2/R4 diverge on PHI/SEA) and should be treated as lower-confidence spots given both MIL and PHI carry strong season marks (68% and 61% respectively) when the model is unanimous — it isn't here.
